text:
anya: Heads-up — I'm prototyping an adaptive blackbox probe throttle to reduce probe-induced autoscaling and SNAT noise. Goal: keep synthetic coverage but avoid probes creating the very load they measure.

maria: +1. Which utilisation signal are you gating on? GPU node-level, pod-level, or aggregate cluster?

devon: we've seen probe bursts in eu-west trigger surge autoscale repeatedly. I'd prefer a region-scoped token bucket keyed by probe-group (embeddings / streaming / health) so one noisy probe type doesn't blow up others.

liam: also add SNAT protection. Probe runners open a ton of short TCP conns for streaming handshakes — that's correlating with ephemeral port exhaustion during sustained tests. Connection reuse + lower RPS will help.

sre-bot: Alert: probe_error_rate_eu-west > 1% for 5m (fired)

anya: proposed policy sketch: default sample_rate = 1r/s per probe-instance. If region_gpu_utilization_percent > 65% for 3m OR inference_stream_handshake_failures_total/5m > 0.5% then scale probe weight to 10% (0.1r/s) for that probe-group/region. Hysteresis: restore after 6m under threshold. Also keep a small canary set of probes (5 hosts) at full rate for coverage.

anya: config snippet (probe-runner config):
```yaml
probe_groups:
  - name: streaming
    default_rate_rps: 1.0
    throttle_policy:
      - condition: "region_gpu_utilization_percent > 65 and sustained_for: 3m"
        new_rate_rps: 0.1
      - condition: "inference_stream_handshake_failures_total_rate > 0.005"
        new_rate_rps: 0.1
    canary_hosts: 5
    max_rps_per_region: 50
  - name: embeddings
    default_rate_rps: 0.5
    throttle_policy: []
```

anya: prometheus recording + alert rules (draft):
```yaml
- record: meta:region_gpu_util_percent:avg5m
  expr: avg by(region) (node_gpu_utilization_percent[5m])

- alert: ProbeThrottleCandidate
  expr: meta:region_gpu_util_percent:avg5m > 65
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: info
  annotations:
    summary: "Region {{ $labels.region }} high GPU util — consider probe throttle"
```

maria: grafana panels to add: "Probe noise vs Real RPS" (sum by(region,kind)(probe_rps) vs sum by(region)(client_rps)), "Probe cost estimate" (approx tokens * probe_rps -> dollars). Add p95 latency and handshake-failures overlay so we can tell if throttling hides a real regression.

devon: two operational notes: 1) keep the canary probes in a different subnet so SNAT effects are visible separately, 2) implement a short-term spike protection token bucket on the HTTP client layer to avoid bursts when many probes start at once.

liam: runbook draft:
- If ProbeThrottleCandidate fires: check probe-runner selfmetrics (probe_run_rate, probe_queue_depth), node GPU util, and cluster autoscaler events.
- If probe throttle active but model-side SLOs (model_p99_latency, model_error_rate) increase: revert throttle and investigate cause.
- If SNAT port exhaustion symptoms (conn_reset spikes, node ephemeral_ports_used > 80%): scale probe runner replicas down to 0.2x and enable connection pooling.

maria: also add alert: model_p99_error_rate_delta > 0.005 for 10m when probes are throttled (so we don't blind ourselves).

anya: I'll open PR with probe-runner changes + prometheus rules. Plan canary rollout in us-west2 first, then eu-west after 48h. Est ETA: PR + tests today, canary tomorrow morning.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: probe-runner v2 -> us-west2 (20% of probe runners)

liam: cost note: fewer probes reduces egress to hosted models and lowers billing for connector requests — estimate ~18% drop for eu-west if we throttle long probes.

devon: we should tag telemetry so we can measure coverage loss: metric probe_coverage_ratio_by_suite{throttled="true|false"}. keep targets above 95%.

anya: good point — will include coverage metric and dashboard. I'll ping when PR is ready. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — love the conservative hysteresis. avoids oscillation.
